issues.detail: The Greek 'ο δε ειπεν' (but he said) is translated as 'Người thưa rằng' (He replied/said). While 'thưa' implies a polite response, the Greek 'δε' (but) indicates a transition or contrast in the narrative flow that is lost in the Vietnamese translation.

The Greek 'ινα αναβλεψω' uses the subjunctive 'ινα', expressing a purpose or request ('so that I may see'). The Vietnamese 'xin cho tôi được sáng mắt lại' adds 'sáng' (bright/clear), which is an interpretive addition not present in the literal Greek 'αναβλεψω' (see again/be able to see).
